subproblem.title: Constancy theorem for integer multiplicity cycles supported in an n-plane: S = c[[Q]] and M_W(S) = |c|·H^n(W ∩ Q)
subproblem.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, every open V ⊆ ℝ^P, every orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) in ℝ^P with Q := span{τ_1, …, τ_n}, and every S ∈ 𝒟_n(V): if S is integer multiplicity, ∂S = 0 in V (BoundaryVanishes S), spt S ⊆ Q and V ∩ Q is connected (in particular nonempty), then there is c ∈ ℤ such that S(ω) = c·∫_{V∩Q} ω(x)(τ_1, …, τ_n) dH^n(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(V) (S = c[[Q]] in V, with Q oriented by τ), and M_W(S) = |c|·H^n(W ∩ Q) for every open W ⊆ V. Here H^n = μHE[n] and |c| = c.natAbs.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn V n) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), 1 ≤ n → IsOpen V → Orthonormal ℝ τ → IsIntegerMultiplicity S → BoundaryVanishes S → S.support ⊆ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P)) → IsConnected (V ∩ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P))) → ∃ c : ℤ, (∀ ω : TestFormOn V n, S ω = (c : ℝ) * ∫ x in V ∩ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P)), (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x τ ∂μHE[n]) ∧ ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → W ⊆ V → S.massOn W = (c.natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) * μHE[n] (W ∩ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the Constancy Theorem, Simon Ch. 6, Theorem 2.34 (and its use for currents carried by a plane in the proof of the deformation theorem, Simon Ch. 6, (26)–(27)), cited by the parent proof in step 4 ("by the constancy theorem (Ch. 6, 2.34) on the connected sets P_i ∖ {0}") and in step 8 ("By constancy (∂C = 0, C integer multiplicity, Π connected), C = c₀[[Π]]"). This version records both conclusions of the theorem: the current identity S = c[[Q]] (used for tangent cones by the sibling children cone_tangent_cone_planar and cone_sector_endpoint_density) and the mass identity. Notation: H^n := μHE[n]; for an integer multiplicity current, the conventions of im_mass_measure (`Submission.dimred_im_mass_measure`) are used. Q := span{τ_1, …, τ_n}; τ is orthonormal, hence a basis of Q, and dim Q = n.
1. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep V n represent S and μ := R.measure = θ·H^n⌞M. By im_mass_measure (a), M_W(S) = μ(W) for every open W ⊆ V; by (b), a point x ∈ V lies outside spt S iff μ(B_ε(x)) = 0 for some ε > 0.
2. μ(V ∖ Q) = 0 and H^n(M ∖ Q) = 0: V ∖ Q is open (Q is closed) and disjoint from spt S, so each of its points has a μ-null ball; by Lindelöf (ℝ^P is second countable) countably many such balls cover V ∖ Q. As M ⊆ V and θ ≥ 1 on M, H^n(M ∖ Q) ≤ μ(M ∖ Q) = 0.
3. Use the given orthonormal basis τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) of Q, the linear isometry ι : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, ι(s) = Σ_i s_iτ_i (image Q), and ξ_Q ∈ Λ_n given by ξ_Q(α) := α(τ_1, …, τ_n). Then H^n⌞Q = ι_#(L^n) (μHE[n] is preserved by isometries and equals Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n; Mathlib `Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image`, `EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`).
4. (Orientation.) By the field `orients`, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ Q there is an n-dimensional Q_x with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_x and ξ(x) = ±(α ↦ α(τ'_x)) for an orthonormal basis τ'_x of Q_x. We claim Q_x = Q. Since H^n(M ∖ Q) = 0, ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dH^n = ∫_{η_{x,r}(M ∩ Q)} f dH^n (H^n(η_{x,r}(M ∖ Q)) = r^{−n}H^n(M ∖ Q) = 0), and η_{x,r}(M ∩ Q) ⊆ Q because x ∈ Q and Q is a subspace. So ∫_{Q_x} f dH^n = 0 for every continuous compactly supported f ≥ 0 vanishing on Q. If Q_x ≠ Q, then Q_x ∩ Q is a proper subspace of Q_x and Q_x ∖ Q contains a nonempty relatively open subset of Q_x, on which a suitable such f is positive; its H^n⌞Q_x-integral is positive, a contradiction. Hence Q_x = Q. Two orthonormal bases of Q differ by an orthogonal matrix A, and α(τ'_x) = det(A)·α(τ) = ±α(τ) for every alternating n-form α. Therefore ξ(x) = ε(x)ξ_Q with ε(x) ∈ {1, −1} for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ Q; ε = ξ(·)(α₀) for any fixed α₀ with α₀(τ) = 1 is H^n⌞M-measurable (ξ is a.e. strongly measurable).
5. Put g := 1_M·ε·θ on Q, an integer-valued H^n⌞Q-measurable function with ∫_{K ∩ Q}|g| dH^n ≤ μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ V. By (2) and (4), for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(V), S(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dH^n = ∫_{V ∩ Q} g(x)⟨ω(x), ξ_Q⟩ dH^n(x), and μ = |g|·H^n⌞(V ∩ Q).
6. (Zero weak derivatives.) Let Ω := ι^{−1}(V) ⊆ ℝ^n (open; ι restricts to a homeomorphism of Ω onto V ∩ Q, so Ω is connected and nonempty) and h := g∘ι ∈ L¹_loc(Ω). Let ψ ∈ C^∞_c(Ω) and i ∈ {1, …, n}. Since ι(spt ψ) is a compact subset of the open set V, there is δ > 0 with {y ∈ ℝ^P : ι^*(y) ∈ spt ψ, |y − p_Q(y)| ≤ δ} ⊆ V, where ι^*(y) := (⟨y, τ_1⟩, …, ⟨y, τ_n⟩) and p_Q is the orthogonal projection onto Q. With χ ∈ C^∞_c(ℝ^P), χ = 1 near 0, spt χ ⊆ B_δ(0), put f(y) := ψ(ι^*(y))·χ(y − p_Q(y)): f ∈ C^∞_c(V), f(ι(s)) = ψ(s) and D_{τ_i}f(ι(s)) = ∂_iψ(s) (the second factor is 1 near Q and τ_i − p_Q(τ_i) = 0). Let α_i := τ_1^♭ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τ_{i−1}^♭ ∧ τ_{i+1}^♭ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τ_n^♭ (τ_j^♭ := ⟨τ_j, ·⟩; for n = 1, α_1 := 1) and φ := f·α_i ∈ 𝒟^{n−1}(V). Then dφ = df ∧ α_i and ⟨dφ(x), ξ_Q⟩ = (df ∧ α_i)(τ_1, …, τ_n) = (−1)^{i−1}D_{τ_i}f(x). Since ∂S = 0 in V, 0 = ∂S(φ) = S(dφ) = (−1)^{i−1}∫_{V ∩ Q} g D_{τ_i}f dH^n = (−1)^{i−1}∫_Ω h(s)∂_iψ(s) ds by (3) and (5).
7. (Constancy.) A function h ∈ L¹_loc(Ω) all of whose weak first derivatives vanish on the connected open set Ω ⊆ ℝ^n is a.e. equal to a constant c: the mollifications h_ε := h ∗ φ_ε are smooth with ∇h_ε = 0 on {s : dist(s, ∂Ω) > ε}, hence locally constant there, and h_ε → h in L¹_loc(Ω), so h is a.e. constant near every point, and connectedness makes the constant global (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 2.34; SimonGMT `WeakDerivativesZero.ae_eq_const`, `ae_eq_const_of_weak_coordinate_derivatives_zero`, Chapter08/DistributionalConstancy.lean). (If a library form of this fact tests against C¹_c functions, note that (6) extends from ψ ∈ C^∞_c(Ω) to ψ ∈ C¹_c(Ω): the mollifications ψ_ε ∈ C^∞_c(Ω) have supports in a fixed compact subset K of Ω for small ε and ∂_iψ_ε → ∂_iψ uniformly, while h is integrable on K, so ∫_Ω h∂_iψ = lim ∫_Ω h∂_iψ_ε = 0.) Since h takes integer values and h = c on a set of positive measure (Ω is open and nonempty), c ∈ ℤ.
8. (Conclusion.) By (7), h = c L^n-a.e. on Ω; since ι maps L^n-null subsets of Ω onto H^n-null subsets of V ∩ Q (by (3)), g = c H^n-a.e. on V ∩ Q. Hence, by (5), for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(V), S(ω) = ∫_{V∩Q} c⟨ω(x), ξ_Q⟩ dH^n(x) = c·∫_{V∩Q} ω(x)(τ_1, …, τ_n) dH^n(x), which is the current identity. Also μ = |g|·H^n⌞(V ∩ Q) = |c|·H^n⌞(V ∩ Q), so for every open W ⊆ V, M_W(S) = μ(W) = |c|·H^n(W ∩ V ∩ Q) = |c|·H^n(W ∩ Q), with |c| = c.natAbs. ∎
proof_key_steps: Represent S by R = (M, θ, ξ); M_W(S) = R.measure(W) on open W ⊆ V and spt S is the support of R.measure in V.
spt S ⊆ Q gives R.measure(V ∖ Q) = 0 (Lindelöf), so H^n(M ∖ Q) = 0.
A.e. on M the approximate tangent plane is Q, so ξ = ±ξ_Q with ξ_Q(α) = α(τ), and S(ω) = ∫_{V∩Q} g⟨ω, ξ_Q⟩ dH^n with g integer-valued and L¹_loc.
∂S = 0 tested on f·α_i (f extending ψ ∈ C^∞_c(ι^{−1}V) off Q) gives zero weak derivatives of g∘ι on the connected open ι^{−1}(V).
Distributional constancy: g = c ∈ ℤ a.e., so S(ω) = c∫_{V∩Q} ω(x)(τ) dH^n, R.measure = |c|·H^n⌞(V ∩ Q) and M_W(S) = |c|·H^n(W ∩ Q).

audit.reason: The type retains openness, positive degree, orthonormality, integer multiplicity, vanishing boundary, support containment and nonempty connectedness. Orientation reduction and distributional constancy establish both the signed current identity and the absolute-multiplicity mass identity.
